messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.m@redwood.ai>

Subject: Next steps: throughput constraints + quick latency remediation plan

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please reply if I've missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Tail and p95 latency spikes during peak windows (notable at model warm-up and burst events)
- Streaming UX jitter for short, interactive responses (users see partial tokens delayed)
- Concurrency limits causing rejected requests (you’re seeing 429s when QPS spikes)
- Current infra: on-prem inference hosts behind an NFS-backed artifact store + Triton 23.x for serving; caching is ad hoc

Measured goals you gave:
- p95 streaming response latency <= 150 ms for 1–2 token interactive responses
- Sustained concurrency target: 50 simultaneous streaming sessions with headroom to 150 during bursts
- Peak QPS target: ~900 sustained during trading-hours spikes

Immediate technical hypotheses (what’s likely causing the pain):
1) KV cache is not warmed / is stored on NFS which causes cold-starts and long tail spikes.
2) Triton config is single-request priority, no continuous batching for streaming.
3) Network egress and serialization overhead in your agent layer adds ~30–80ms variance.

Proposed short-term plan (scope: discovery -> pilot -> measurement):
- Week 0: Exchange anonymized perf traces (request ids, timestamps) and a 5-minute sampling window of production traffic. You mentioned you can provide 48 hours of sampling logs; that will let us validate the hypothesis re: KV cold starts.
- Week 1: Redwood SRE + Finlytics infra run a focused latency baseline: 30-minute soak at expected peak QPS (900) against a shadow endpoint we’ll host. Deliverable: p95/p99 baseline report. (Attachment: latency-test-plan.xlsx)
- Week 2: Pilot with lightweight prefix/KV caching (we’ll deploy a caching proxy) and tuned batching parameters. Deliverable: quantifiable p95 improvement and CPU/GPU utilization delta.

Commercial/ops asks you flagged:
- Cost ballpark for a 2-week pilot + projected monthly unit economics if we meet SLOs (we’ll prepare this once we have baseline metrics).
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned an internal review in mid-May.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa will draft the test plan and a runbook.
- I’ll prepare a short MOP (method of procedure) for the shadow test and include rollback steps. (Attachment: redwood-mop-overview.pdf)
- Proposed meeting: Thu 15 Apr, 11:00am PT for kickoff and to exchange logs — open to other times.

Attachments: redwood-mop-overview.pdf (overview, rollback), latency-test-plan.xlsx (test matrix + telemetry checklist)

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Aditya Rao

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>

Thanks Aditya — accurate summary. A few clarifications and additions from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Our real-world peak is actually a 15-minute rolling average near 900 qps; short bursts to ~1.4k QPS for a minute or two during market events.
- Model family: mainly 7B decoder-only, mixed-precision quantized weights. Token length is typically very short (1–5 tokens) because agents return single-step completions.
- Current infra detail: Triton runs on a 4xA100 on-prem cluster. Model artifacts are stored on central NFS; workers mount models per-request which we suspect causes I/O stalls.

Procurement / timeline:
- We have a procurement review window 13–20 May. If the pilot shows a measurable improvement, we can accelerate to an initial procurement decision by end of May.

Data we can share this week:
- 48 hours of anonymized request traces (timestamps + request id + model size + observed end-to-end latency).
- A sample GPU utilization report for peak windows.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm whether the shadow endpoint will require any firewall/VPN changes on our side?
2) What telemetry fields do you absolutely need in the trace export (we’ll scrub PII)?

We’re happy with Thu 15 Apr 11:00am PT for kickoff.

Thanks,
Alex
CTO, Finlytics
